chapters.title: 1. Introduction to Book-Keeping and Accountancy
chapters.notes:
Book-keeping is the systematic recording of financial transactions. Accountancy also includes classifying, summarising, analysing and interpreting financial information.

Key terms:
• Capital: amount invested by owner.
• Drawings: cash or goods taken by owner for personal use.
• Assets: resources owned or controlled by a business.
• Liabilities: amounts payable by the business.
• Debtor: a person who owes money to the business.
• Creditor: a person to whom the business owes money.

chapters.title: 1. Introduction to Commerce and Business
chapters.notes:
Commerce includes trade and aids to trade. Trade means buying and selling goods or services. Aids to trade include transport, banking, insurance, warehousing, advertising and communication.

Business objectives may be economic (profit, growth, innovation) and social (quality goods, fair prices, employment and environmental responsibility).

chapters.title: 1. Introduction to Secretarial Practice
chapters.notes:
Secretarial practice includes communication, record keeping, meeting support and administrative procedures. Useful qualities include accuracy, confidentiality, punctuality, organisation and communication skills.

chapters.title: 1. Basic Concepts in Economics
chapters.notes:
Economics studies how people and society use limited resources to satisfy wants. Scarcity leads to choice. Opportunity cost is the next-best alternative given up when a choice is made.

Microeconomics studies individual consumers, firms and markets. Macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole.
